 Bhopal BJP Rally: Schools Holiday Declared | Nadda Visit & Patwari Protest
 BJP's march in Bhopal tomorrow, three schools to remain closed: Union Minister JP Nadda to attend; Jitu Patwari asks why children should bear the brunt of the BJP rally
 Bhopal 8 hours ago 
 Copy link 
 Three schools in Bhopal have declared a holiday on Wednesday, November 4, due to the BJP's 'Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy' march in the city.
 St Joseph's, St Thomas and St Xavier's schools have announced the holiday, keeping in mind the safety of students and possible travel problems. Other schools may also review the situation and decide whether to declare a holiday or change their timings.
 A public meeting will be held at 10 am on Atal Path in TT Nagar, in the presence of Union Minister JP Nadda. After the meeting, the march will pass through New Market and reach Roshanpura Square.
 A large number of people are expected to attend the programme from the Bhopal and Narmadapuram divisions. This may affect traffic on several main roads in the city.
 Congress state president Jitu Patwari has criticised the BJP's march and the decision to declare school holidays or change timings. He questioned why children and parents should suffer because of the BJP's rally.
 Schools asked to take decisions independently 
 In an order issued on November 3, the District Education Officer (DEO) asked all government and private schools in the district to assess the situation, including the routes used by students and the movement of school buses.
 Based on this assessment, schools have been asked to decide whether to change their timings or suspend classes on November 4 to ensure that students do not face travel problems.
 School managements have also been directed to inform parents, students and vehicle operators about their decisions. They must also send the information to the DEO's office.
 The district education officer has written to all schools. Traffic jams likely on routes to schools 
 According to the traffic police, an estimated 40,000 to 50,000 people are expected to attend the programme. The BJP has claimed that around one lakh people will arrive.
 As many as 1,200 buses and 2,000 four-wheelers are likely to travel to Bhopal for the event. Traffic pressure may increase from 8 a.m. around Bhadbhada Square, Bharat Mata Square, Jawahar Chowk, Mata Mandir, Roshanpura, Link Road 1 and Polytechnic Square.
 As a result, students of schools located on or near these routes may face difficulties commuting. School managements have been specifically asked to make decisions keeping bus routes, students' arrival times and safe travel in mind.
 Post made by Jitu Patwari. Jitu Patwari targets BJP 
 Congress state president Jitu Patwari criticised the move after the Bhopal DEO issued the order. In a post on his X account, Patwari wrote, "Why should parents bear the brunt of the BJP rally?"
 Foot march from Atal Path to Roshanpura 
 Union Minister JP Nadda, Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav and BJP state president Hemant Khandelwal will address the rally. After the rally, the foot march will begin at Atal Path and proceed through New Market to Roshanpura Square. Welcome platforms will be set up along the route by doctors, lawyers, engineers, various social and caste-based groups, as well as the third-gender community.
 Separate routes and parking for buses 
 The traffic police have designated routes, passenger drop-off points and parking areas for buses arriving from outside. On the return journey, buses will pick up passengers only from the designated parking areas.
 Vidisha-Raisen: Passengers will get off at Patel Nagar, Khajuri Kalan T-junction, Piplani Road, Mahatma Gandhi Square, Chetak Bridge, Board Office and Link Road-1, and near Apex Bank and TT Cross, before reaching TT Nagar Stadium. Parking will be available at the LLA Rest House premises.
 Narmadapuram-Mandideep-Misrod: Passengers will get off at Narmadapuram Road, Savarkar Bridge, Ganesh Temple, Mansarovar T-junction, Link Road-2, Arjun Nagar, Second Stop and Tulsi Nagar, near Atal Path. Parking will be available near Ambedkar Park, Tulsi Nagar.
 Sehore-Ratibad-Neelbad: Passengers will get off at Ratibad, Neelbad, Sakhi Dhaba T-junction, Bhadbhada and Bharat Mata Square, and at Jawahar Chowk. Parking will be available at Model School.
 Mubarakpur Bypass: Passengers will disembark at Kamla Nehru School Centre Point via Mubarakpura, Gandhinagar, Lalghati, VIP Road, Polytechnic, Banganga and Rangmahal. Parking will be around the TT Nagar Dussehra Ground.
 Old City: Passengers will disembark near the TT Nagar Stadium via Bharat Talkies, Lily Square, Control Room, Gandhi Park and Roshanpura. Parking will be at Lal Parade Ground, Ravindra Bhavan and Khatlapura Road.
